author: YonsiG
body:
#### PR description:

In `HGCalRawToDigi::produce`, the three host SoA collections (`digis`, `econdPacketInfo`, `fedPacketInfo`) are allocated with a size taken from the module indexer, i.e. the maximum possible number of modules / channels / FEDs. The unpacker then fills only the rows that correspond to data actually present in the FED payload. Rows (and columns) it never writes keep whatever was left in the allocated memory, so the products contain non-deterministic, uninitialised values.

This PR zero-initialises the three collections right after allocation with `zeroInitialise()`.

Expected changes in the output:
- Entries written by the unpacker: unchanged.
- Entries not written by the unpacker: now always zero instead of leftover memory.
- As a consequence the output is reproducible from run to run, and it compresses much better, since the uninitialised entries were effectively random bytes.

#### PR validation:

Ran runTheMatrix workflow 77 on an HGCal test-beam sample ([N] events) three times before the fix and three times after it, writing the three SoA products with LZMA level 4:

- All entries written by the unpacker are identical before and after the fix; only the previously uninitialised entries changed (to zero).
- Before the fix the compressed size differs from run to run, showing the content was not reproducible. After the fix the three runs are identical.
- The uncompressed size is unchanged, as the buffer capacity is the same.

Compressed size per event (B/event, LZMA 4):

| Product | Uncompressed | Before fix (run 1 / 2 / 3) | After fix (runs 13) | Reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| SoA digis | 29,347 | 3,102 / 4,441 / 3,966 | 2,160 | 30% to 51% |
| FED packet info | 40,549 | 3,615 / 3,429 / 7,535 | 661 | 81% to 91% |
| ECON-D packet info | 3,676 | 590 / 566 / 771 | 496 | 12% to 36% |
| **Total** | **73,572** | **7,306 / 8,435 / 12,271** | **3,316** | **55% to 73%** |

`scram b`, `scram b code-checks` and `scram b code-format` pass.
title: Zero initialization to hgcalDigis variables
